annotationRationale: The question asks for an exact category count in sampling without replacement. The primary method counts unordered selections; the alternative multiplies conditional draw probabilities and counts match-position patterns.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: For any fixed Harold selection, Betty has \(\binom{10}{5}=252\) equally likely sets, with \(\binom52\binom53=100\) sharing exactly two books. The probability is \(25/63\), choice D, consistent with the key. No question, choice, or figure contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The unordered-selection and sequential conditional-probability routes are both useful and retained. The supplied joint-selection count is another decomposition of the same combination count and does not require an additional method.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed sampling-without-replacement category count fits cnm_h257's stated criteria; no distribution theorem is needed. Combinations are appropriate support, and the sequential method directly identifies conditional multiplication.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Fixing Harold leaves two groups of five regardless of his particular selection. Choosing two from his group and three from its complement gives 100 uniquely counted favorable sets among 252 equally likely sets. Their ratio simplifies to \(25/63\).
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE and AoPS Solution 1 support this route. The source-informed-original designation is correct, and the explanation independently develops the symmetry, notation, and unique-count justification.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why Harold's random choice can be fixed. Combination notation is defined, the two category choices enforce exactly two shared books, and the favorable-to-total ratio is justified.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h257 matches an exact category-count probability under sampling without replacement. cnm_h239 precisely captures the unordered choices and product of category counts.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: Both exact CN topic links fit. The solution computes one without-replacement probability, but does not establish the separate criterion of distinguishing hypergeometric from binomial sampling.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower S-CP.B.9 link supports the combination-based compound probability. No accepted US link is supplied for cnm_h257, so a full distribution alignment should not be inferred.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: Both immediate IDs are justified by the elementary counting derivation. The distribution label does not introduce an advanced prerequisite into the explanation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: For the stated match-match-nonmatch-nonmatch-nonmatch pattern, the conditional factors multiply to \(5/126\). Every two-match pattern has the same numerator factors and denominator factors. The ten disjoint position patterns therefore give \(10(5/126)=25/63\).
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solution 2 supplies the sequential-pattern idea but contains an incorrect displayed probability product. The candidate transparently identifies that defect and independently derives correct factors, consistent with source-informed-original status.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: Equal numbers of draw orders justify modeling a uniform set by sequential draws. The factors, equal pattern probabilities, ten position choices, and disjointness are all explained.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h245 directly captures successive conditional multiplication, and cnm_h239 captures choosing the two match positions. Both are actually used.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: cnm_h245's partial CN link fits ordered conditional multiplication; all conditioning events used here have positive probability. cnm_h239's exact topic link fits the ten unordered position choices.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The broader S-CP.B.8 link applies through this uniform sequential model, although the general canonical rule has wider scope. The narrower S-CP.B.9 link supports the combination count of match positions. Neither application establishes every part of those standards.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The two direct nodes precisely describe the probability product and pattern count. They support the question's without-replacement target without invoking a distribution formula.
